options.metric: Annual count of pedestrians injured in reported crashes
options.reason: Injury counts give readers a direct measure of the reported nonfatal harm to pedestrians over time.
options.answer: Reported pedestrian injuries were lower in 2025 than in 2013 (2,835 vs. 3,641; down 22%), although they rose from 1,781 in 2020. The data cannot establish whether risk per walking trip improved because it contains no pedestrian-exposure measure.

options.metric: Annual count of pedestrians killed in reported crashes
options.reason: Fatality counts isolate the most severe outcome and make clear that an injury-count decline need not mean fewer deaths.
options.answer: Pedestrian deaths were higher in 2025 than in 2013 (39 vs. 30; up 30%), with substantial year-to-year variation. The data cannot establish whether risk per walking trip improved because it contains no pedestrian-exposure measure.

options.metric: Share of Brooklyn crash records with at least one pedestrian injured or killed
options.denominator: All police-reported Brooklyn crash records in that year
options.reason: A share of reported crashes adds context when the overall number of crash records changes substantially over time.
options.answer: Crashes with a pedestrian injury or death rose from 7.4% of Brooklyn crash records in 2013 to 11.4% in 2025. The data cannot establish whether risk per walking trip improved because it contains no pedestrian-exposure measure.
